title: Passport to Access, Change, Vendor & Travel Operations
author: Maria Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook consolidates company-wide operational policies for access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding/management, and travel. It provides prescriptive workflows, approval matrices, owners, and reusable templates for consistent execution across teams.

Scope
-----
Applies to: All Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with Redwood systems or representing Redwood externally.
Applies to systems: Cloud accounts, on-prem infrastructure, Redwood Console, internal business systems (finance, HR, ticketing), and private deployments where Redwood personnel provide support.
Exclusions: Tactical team-level processes that do not touch company identity, financial approvals, or customer-sensitive data.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege by default: Roles must grant the minimum permissions needed for the job.
- Explicit approval trail: All access, changes, and vendor contracts must be traceable to an approver.
- Risk-based controls: Higher-sensitivity assets require stronger controls (MFA, periodic certification, contractual SLAs).
- Periodic review: Access and vendor risk assessments on a defined cadence.

Roles & Ownership (quick reference)
-------------------------------
- People Ops: Access policy governance, onboarding/offboarding audit, role catalog maintenance.
- Security: RBAC design, privileged access reviews, vendor security questionnaires.
- Finance & Legal: Procurement thresholds, contract sign-off, vendor PO issuance.
- Team Leads: Day-to-day access approvers, change approvers within scope, expense approvers.
- IT/Platform: Implement access grants (IAM), change rollouts for infra services, monitoring.
- Vendor Manager: Vendor onboarding, SLA tracking, quarterly business reviews (QBRs).

Access & Permissions
--------------------
Policy summary:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is the default. No permanent user-level "root" accounts; break-glass exceptions require formal approval.
- MFA is required for all interactive accounts; keys rotating every 90 days for service principals.
- Sensitive resource classification: Confidential (customer PII, private keys), Internal, Public. Confidential resources require two-step approval.

Onboarding flow (standard user)
1. Request: Team lead fills Access Request Template (see Appendix). Submit via ticketing system with business justification.
2. Approval: People Ops + Team Lead sign-off for standard roles. Security review required for access to Confidential resources.
3. Provisioning: IT/Platform uses iamctl to create role bindings. Example commands:
   - iamctl create-role-binding --principal user:alice@redwood.ai --role data-analyst --scope project:telemetry
   - iamctl grant --service-account svc-reporting --role read-only-storage
4. Record: Ticket updated with grant details and entitlement expiration if temporary.

Temporary elevated access & emergency escalation
- Temporary access is granted for a maximum of 7 days by default. Extensions require re-approval.
- Emergency (break-glass) process:
  1) Engineer requests emergency access via the incident channel, tagging security and oncall.
  2) Security issues a one-time ephemeral token (valid 2 hours) and logs the request in the incident ticket.
  3) Post-incident: Owner must file a retrospective and certify that temporary credentials were revoked within 24 hours.

Periodic reviews
- Quarterly role entitlement review (People Ops + Team Leads).
- High-privilege users review every 30 days (Security owner).
- Automation: iamctl export-entitlements --since 90d | ./scripts/entitlement-audit.sh

Change Management
-----------------
Change types:
- Standard: Pre-approved, low-risk routine changes (config tweaks, minor infra scaling) executed via CI with no extra approval.
- Normal: Planned changes that require RFC, owner approval, and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency: Unplanned changes to restore service (follow emergency access flow above).

Approval matrix (examples)
- Low risk (<$5k impact, non-customer facing): Team Lead approval.
- Medium risk (>= $5k or customer-facing impact): Team Lead + Platform owner.
- High risk (security or PII impact, infra changes affecting >1 region): Team Lead + Security + Platform + People Ops for communications.

Change request process (normal change)
1. Create RFC in the change registry with: description, rollback plan, test plan, impact window, owner.
2. Review: Platform/Service owner performs technical review within 48 hours.
3. Approve: Approvals collected (digital sign-off in the ticketing system).
4. Schedule: Schedule in maintenance calendar and notify affected stakeholders 72 hours prior.
5. Execute & Validate: Runbook executed, smoke tests, and post-deploy verification.
6. Close: Post-change report filed within 24 hours of completion.

Emergency changes
- Tag RFC as EMERGENCY and follow 2-hour post-incident postmortem SLA. Root cause and mitigations must be documented.

Data Management
---------------
Classification levels:
- Confidential: Customer PII, private keys, audit logs. Encryption at rest + access limited to named roles. Retention policy: default 7 years for audit logs, PII retention per contract.
- Internal: Company emails, internal metrics. Retention: 2 years unless business need.
- Public: Marketing materials, public docs. No special retention.

Handling rules:
- Confidential data must not be used in development environments without masking. Use synthetic datasets or the data-masking service (maskit).
- Backups containing Confidential data must be encrypted and stored in the locked vault bucket (s3://redwood-vault).
- Data access requests for Confidential data require Data Steward approval and a documented business justification.

Data deletion and retention
- Data deletion requests are processed by the Data Steward team within 30 calendar days.
- Retention exceptions require approval from Legal + Data Steward and must be logged.

Procurement & Expenses
----------------------
Approval thresholds (examples)
- <$1,000: Team Lead approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Team Lead + Finance reviewer.
- >$25,000: Finance + Legal + VP-level approval.

Procurement flow (vendor goods/services)
1. Requisition: Requester files a Purchase Request (PR) with justification, cost center, and preferred vendor.
2. Finance review: Finance validates budget availability and assigns a PO number for approved requests.
3. Legal review: For contracts > $25k or handling Confidential data, Legal performs standard review.
4. PO issuance & payment: Accounts payable issues PO and processes payment upon invoice receipt.

Expense policy highlights
- Travel: Book through approved travel partner or travel@redwood.ai. Personal upgrades must be paid out-of-pocket.
- Per diem: US domestic: $75/day; International: country-dependent (see Appendix).
- Receipt requirements: All expenses >$25 require scanned receipt.

Vendor Management
-----------------
Onboarding checklist
1. Vendor intake form submitted (business case, contact, services provided).
2. Security questionnaire (SIG-lite) completed and reviewed by Security.
3. Contract terms reviewed by Legal (include data residency, breach notification SLA, indemnity).
4. PO or contract signed and linked to vendor record.
5. Vendor added to vendor registry and scheduled for first QBR within 90 days.

SLAs & monitoring
- Standard vendor SLA expectations: 99.5% uptime for production services, 24h initial response for critical incidents.
- Vendor Manager maintains vendor scorecard: availability, response SLAs, quarterly NPS.

Offboarding
- Termination checklist: confirm data return or secure deletion, revoke credentials, close open POs, final invoice reconciliation, document lessons learned.

Travel Policy (summary)
----------------------
Booking rules
- Use corporate travel portal for flights/hotels. Exceptions require manager approval.
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours; premium economy allowed for flights > 6 hours with approval.

Reimbursement and per diem
- Use expense system to submit within 30 days of travel.
- Meals and incidental receipts must be itemized for claims above per diem.

Health & safety
- Employees traveling to high-risk countries must register with People Ops and complete safety training.
- Company will not approve travel to locations flagged in the Travel Risk Matrix without exec sign-off.

Communications & Templates
-------------------------
Included templates (copyable):
- Access Request Template (fields: requester, role, justification, expiry)
- Vendor Risk Assessment checklist (SIG-lite excerpt)
- Change Request (RFC) template with rollback steps and smoke tests
- Travel approval form with destination risk and itinerary summary

Appendix A — Access Request Template (example)
---------------------------------------------
Requester: __________________
Team: ______________________
Requested role(s): ___________
Business justification: _______
Requested duration (if temporary): __days
Approvals: Team Lead / Security (if needed) / People Ops

Appendix B — Vendor Risk Assessment (excerpt)
--------------------------------------------
- Does vendor store Confidential data? (Y/N)
- Data residency requirements satisfied? (Y/N)
- Has vendor completed SOC2 or equivalent? (Y/N)
- Incident notification SLA <= 72 hours? (Y/N)
- PII handling: encryption at rest/in transit? (Y/N)

Appendix C — Sample RFC YAML
---------------------------
```yaml
id: RFC-2025-045
title: Migrate telemetry workers to new autoscaler
owner: samira@redwood.ai
risk: medium
impact_window: 2025-08-14T01:00Z/2025-08-14T03:00Z
rollback_steps:
  - scale down new autoscaler
  - revert deployment image to v1.12.2
smoke_tests:
  - curl -f https://telemetry.redwood.ai/health
  - check metrics: telemetry_items_processed > 100/min after 10m
approvals: [team_lead, platform_owner]
```

Operational SLAs & KPIs
----------------------
- Access provisioning: 95% of standard role requests fulfilled within 2 business days.
- Change review SLA: Technical review completed within 48 hours for planned changes.
- Vendor QBR cadence: first QBR within 90 days of onboarding; quarterly thereafter.

Governance & Exceptions
----------------------
- Exceptions to these policies require documented approval from People Ops + Security + Finance, and must include a sunset date.
- Noncompliance escalations: team lead -> department head -> People Ops -> Legal. Repeated violations may result in access suspension.

How to use this playbook
------------------------
- Copy templates from the Appendix to create tickets.
- Follow the approval matrix above; when in doubt, escalate to Security or People Ops.
- For system-level changes, create an RFC and reference this playbook in the ticket.

Document maintenance
--------------------
Owner: People Ops
Review cadence: Annual full review; targeted updates when regulatory or business changes occur.
Change log: See page history for detailed edits.

Contacts
--------
- People Ops (access policy): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security (privileged access): security@redwood.ai
- Finance (procurement): procurement@redwood.ai
- Vendor Management: vendors@redwood.ai
